label: Late encoding / <DEL> step in sequences whose first two tokens come from {g,u,p,i,2,3,b,h}
explanation: Fires almost only at the <DEL> step (65% of activation mass, 7.4x lift) and at later original-phase steps (t>=3, first occurrences of a token); it is essentially silent at t<2 and through the copy phase (1% of mass). Whether it fires depends on which tokens opened the sequence: first token g/u/p/i/2/3 gives 3-5x lift, and requiring the first two tokens both to be in {g,u,p,i,2,3,b,h} raises <DEL>-step precision to about 0.67. The largest activations are short sequences like u 3 h k <DEL> or g u p u <DEL>. Later tokens such as m, z, x, c, s, q seem to suppress it, and repeated tokens rarely fire. It reads as a distributed readout of prefix composition, and no simple predicate gets past about 0.34 F1 on dev. Magnitude claims were checked only against the top examples.
